disease_label_per_paper: Acute cytomegalovirus hepatitis in an immunocompetent patient
presentation_summary: 35-year-old immunocompetent man presented with 1 week of intermittent fever and constitutional symptoms.
Symptoms included chills, malaise, myalgia, headache, mild sore throat, and diarrhea, without cough, dyspnea, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dysuria, or urinary frequency.
Admission vitals were stable with temperature 37.8 C, pulse 90/min, respiratory rate 20/min, and normal blood pressure; fever later spiked to 39 C in the first 3 hospital days.
Initial labs showed WBC 6.59 x10^9/L with lymphocytes 63.7%, neutrophils 12.7%, AST 396 U/L, ALT 505 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 204 U/L, and GGT 174 U/L.
Ultrasound showed splenic long-axis 11.4 cm with splenomegaly; day-4 CBC showed WBC 14.12 x10^9/L with 70.8% lymphocytes and 0.9% atypical lymphocytes.

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Serological tests for viral hepatitis A, B, C, herpes simplex, and Epstein-Barr virus were all negative; antinuclear antibody, antismooth muscle antibody, and antimitochondrial antibody levels were negative; HIV rapid test was also negative

actual_treatment: symptomatic management without CMV antiviral therapy
piperacillin-tazobactam empirically until bacterial infection was excluded
quality_warnings: CMV IgM and CMV PCR are stored in confirmatory_findings, not ordinary observations.
Day-4 atypical lymphocyte fraction is included in lab_trajectories because it was reported after admission but before any CMV antiviral therapy.
Normal hemoglobin, platelet count, bilirubin, and prothrombin time were reported without numeric values, so they were not encoded as numeric observations.
